biological.citation: Bidirectional histone monoaminylation dynamics regulate neural rhythmicity (PMID: 39779849)
biological.summary: H3Q5 histaminylation (H3Q5his) inhibits the binding of WDR5, a core member of histone H3 Lys4 (H3K4) methyltransferase complexes, thereby antagonizing methyltransferase activities on H3K4. This represents a mechanism by which histone monoaminylation regulates chromatin state through modulation of WDR5 binding. The finding was demonstrated in brain tissue in the context of diurnally rhythmic gene expression.

biological.citation: WDR5 represents a therapeutically exploitable target for cancer stem cells in glioblastoma (PMID: 36732025)
biological.summary: WDR5 was identified as indispensable for the SOX2-enriched, therapy-resistant cancer stem cell (CSC) niche in GBM patient-derived organoids via a spatially resolved loss-of-function screen. WDR5 inhibitors blocked WRAD complex assembly, reduced H3K4 trimethylation, and disrupted CSC in vitro growth, self-renewal, and in vivo tumor growth. H3K4me3 peaks lost upon WDR5 inhibition were disproportionately associated with POU transcription factor motifs including the OCT4::SOX2 motif.

biological.citation: MLL/WDR5 complex recruits centriolar satellite protein Cep72 to regulate microtubule nucleation and spindle formation (PMID: 39661677)
biological.summary: WDR5, as part of the MLL/WDR5 complex, localizes to the pericentriolar material and interacts with centriolar satellite protein Cep72 and γ-tubulin ring complex proteins (γ-TuRCs), revealing a non-epigenetic role at the centrosome. Loss of WDR5 impairs microtubule nucleation and regrowth, affects spindle formation, and leads to misaligned chromosomes during mitosis. MLL and WDR5 recruit Cep72 to the centrosome, and this phenotype is also observed in cells from patients with Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome.

MYC oncoproteins interact directly with WDR5, a WD40-repeat protein component of chromatin-regulatory complexes, to create an avidity-based chromatin recognition mechanism that allows MYC to select target genes in response to both genetic and epigenetic determinants. This interaction provides plasticity in MYC target gene selection and is proposed to occur in the context of WDR5's role in multiple chromatin-regulatory complexes. The MYC-WDR5 interface is highlighted as an attractive target for small-molecule inhibitors of MYC function in cancer.

biological.citation: MBD2 regulates the progression and chemoresistance of cholangiocarcinoma through interaction with WDR5 (PMID: 39350229)
biological.summary: MBD2 directly interacts with WDR5 and binds to the ABCB1 promoter, promoting H3K4 trimethylation via KMT2A and activating ABCB1 expression to drive chemoresistance in cholangiocarcinoma. Knockdown of WDR5 or KMT2A blocked MBD2-mediated transcriptional activation of ABCB1. The WDR5-KMT2A interaction inhibitor MM-102 suppressed ABCB1 expression and decreased CCA chemoresistance to cisplatin in cell and xenograft models.

biological.citation: Targeting WDR5/ATAD2 signaling by the CK2/IKAROS axis demonstrates therapeutic efficacy in T-ALL (PMID: 39785511)
biological.summary: WDR5 is highly expressed in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) and plays an oncogenic role by activating cell cycle signaling through its downstream effector ATAD2. IKAROS directly regulates WDR5 transcription, and CK2 inhibition with CX-4945 suppresses WDR5 expression by restoring IKAROS function. Combining CX-4945 with a WDR5 inhibitor showed synergistic antileukemic efficacy in patient-derived xenograft mouse models.

biological.citation: lncRNA VELRP Modulates Pulmonary Arterial Smooth Muscle Cell Proliferation and Promotes Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension (PMID: 39360410)
biological.summary: The lncRNA VELRP interacts with WDR5 to enhance H3K4 trimethylation, leading to increased expression of CDK1, CDK2, and CDK4 and consequent hyperproliferation of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). This WDR5-dependent epigenetic mechanism was validated by RNA immunoprecipitation and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays. In vivo, smooth muscle cell-specific knockdown of VELRP reduced right ventricular systolic pressure and vascular remodeling in rat pulmonary hypertension models.

biological.citation: Direct mapping of ligandable tyrosines and lysines in cells with chiral sulfonyl fluoride probes (PMID: 37460812)
biological.summary: A chemoproteomic screen using enantiomeric pairs of clickable arylsulfonyl fluoride probes identified Y228 in the MYC binding site of WDR5 as a ligandable residue in intact cells. A high-resolution crystal structure confirmed covalent modification of Y228 by a chiral probe. This finding provides a covalent chemical probe targeting the WDR5-MYC interaction interface for potential therapeutic development.

biological.citation: STING mediates hepatocyte pyroptosis in liver fibrosis by Epigenetically activating the NLRP3 inflammasome (PMID: 37018971)
biological.summary: WDR5 and DOT1L were identified as regulators of NLRP3 expression in STING-overexpressing hepatocytes, where WDR5/DOT1L-mediated histone methylation enhances IRF3 binding to the Nlrp3 promoter and promotes STING-induced Nlrp3 transcription. This defines a STING-WDR5/DOT1L/IRF3-NLRP3 epigenetic signaling axis in hepatocyte pyroptosis and liver fibrosis. The pathway was validated in primary murine hepatocytes and in vivo fibrotic liver models.

biological.citation: Targeting IP(6) signaling to destabilize homologous recombination proteins to overcome PARP inhibitor resistance (PMID: 41935081)
biological.summary: WDR5 was identified as a DCAF (DDB1- and CUL4-associated factor) protein that facilitates Cul4A-mediated proteolysis of RAD51 and CHK1, revealing a novel non-epigenetic role for WDR5 in regulating homologous recombination protein stability. This Cul4A-WDR5-dependent proteolysis pathway is activated by reduction of inositol hexaphosphate (IP6) levels via PIKfyve/PIP5K1C inhibition. Functionally, this mechanism suppresses homologous recombination and enhances tumor sensitivity to PARP inhibitors in vitro and in xenograft models.
